title: Financial-services visibility and access control for AI apps with Hypershield and AI Defense
titleEn: Financial-services visibility and access control for AI apps with Hypershield and AI Defense
fidelityNote: A planning scenario composed from Cisco's public AI Defense and Hypershield material, placed under financial-services constraints. It is not a bank's results. No customer name, quote, or measured MTTR is stored here.
executiveSummary: A financial institution wants to see which AI applications touch customer and transaction data, and to control that access, before any enforce mode. The public ingredients are AI Defense for discovery and runtime protection, and Hypershield for distributed enforcement with a dual data plane so a policy can be observed before it is enforced. The PM plan is a shadow-mode pilot, a rollback, and a separate decision to enforce. Minutes-to-mitigate is a published product design goal, not a measured customer result.
problemStatement: AI applications in a bank cross model providers, lines of business, and the data center. Security can see the network and still not see which application is an AI application, or which one is unapproved. Turning on enforcement before the inventory exists blocks legitimate work and still misses the unknown app.
opportunity: Cisco's public Hypershield design describes enforcement close to the workload and upgrades that qualify themselves on a dual data plane. AI Defense adds discovery of shadow and approved AI, model validation, and runtime controls. Together they give a sequence: discover, observe, then decide whether to enforce.
strategicAlignment: The control objective is visibility and a reversible policy, aligned to electronic-financial supervision, privacy, and credit-information duties. Speed of mitigation is not the acceptance test.
businessValue: The sponsor can point at an inventory, an observation report, and a written enforce-or-hold decision. The program does not claim a percentage reduction in MTTR.
regulatoryContext: Regulation on Supervision of Electronic Financial Transactions
architecturePattern: AI Defense discovers applications and watches runtime use. Hypershield places enforcement in the data center and cloud fabric. New policy runs in shadow on the second data plane. Enforcement waits for the CISO's decision. Talos informs detection. Splunk is the investigation store only if it is already deployed.
planningBandNote: The 750,000 to 2,500,000 US dollar range and the week ranges are planning bands for a first financial pilot. They are not a quote and not a bank's spend.
scopeIn: One business line and the AI applications that touch its data
An inventory of approved and unapproved AI applications
A written decision before enforce mode
scopeOut: Naming a bank that has not been named in the input

outcomes: Planning outcome: an inventory and a shadow-mode report for one business line. This is not a published customer result.
Published design goal: Hypershield describes mitigation in minutes and self-qualifying upgrades on a dual data plane. That is Cisco's product design, not a measured bank outcome.
Published fact: AI Defense, announced 15 January 2025, covers discovery, validation, runtime protection, and access control.

narrative.heading: Public material, financial constraints
narrative.body:
On 18 April 2024 Cisco described Hypershield as distributed security for the AI-scale data center, with enforcement close to workloads and upgrades that can be qualified on a dual data plane before they carry traffic. On 15 January 2025 Cisco described AI Defense as discovery, model validation, runtime protection, and access control for enterprise AI.

This scenario places those two public designs in one financial-services pilot. The regulation set is the Korean electronic-financial supervision rule, the Personal Information Protection Act, and the Credit Information Act, plus NIST AI RMF and the OWASP LLM Top 10 as the control references. Nothing in the public posts is a bank's measured result, so this record does not add one.

The sequence is inventory, shadow mode, observation report, then a CISO decision. Splunk is the investigation store only when it is already there. Talos is the threat intelligence the product posts name.

narrative.heading: What the draft is allowed to say
narrative.body: Say which business line, what was observed, and whether the CISO held or enforced. Do not say a bank name that was not in the request. Do not say an MTTR percentage. If the product phrase about minutes appears, label it as Cisco's design goal and cite the April 2024 post.
